sections.html:
Richardson County occupies the southeast corner of Nebraska. Missouri is across the river to the east and Kansas lies south, and the state's lowest point is where the Missouri leaves Nebraska. Of the county's 555 square miles, most is farmed. The Big Nemaha River and its branches cross the rolling hills on their way to the Missouri.

Falls City is the county seat, and Humboldt is the other city. Eight villages fill out the map: Barada, Dawson, Preston, Rulo, Salem, Shubert, Stella and Verdon. Parts of the Ioway and Sac and Fox reservations lie in the southeast corner, and the village of Preston is inside the Sac and Fox reservation. For a parcel near that area, ask the assessor and a title company how it is classified before you list.

The 2020 census counted 7,871 residents. Median age was 47.2, and 24.9% of residents were 65 or older. An heir who lives out of state and inherits a house in Dawson, Stella or Verdon owes the same tax on the same dates as a neighbor.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects the tax
sections.html:
The treasurer sits at 1700 Stone Street, Room 105, Falls City, NE 68355, and answers at 402-245-3511. MIPS Inc. runs the online system for current and back real estate tax. A card costs 2.35 percent with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check costs $1.00.

Drainage taxes cannot go through that system. Ask the treasurer for the complete balance, drainage items included, before you fix a closing date.

StepDate or rule
First half delinquentMay 1 (Statute 77-204)
Second half delinquentSeptember 1
Valuation protestOn or before June 30, with the County Clerk
Board decision mailedBy August 2
Appeal to the state commissionBy August 24
County tax saleFirst Monday in March, 9:00 a.m.

Find the assessor at 1700 Stone Street, Room 102, or call 402-245-4012, weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., through lunch. The office sets fair and equitable value on real and personal property, keeps parcel maps and prepares the tax roll that the treasurer bills from. Staff attend every Board of Equalization meeting and review homestead exemption applications as well as religious, charitable and educational exemptions.

Form 422 goes to the County Clerk by June 30, one per parcel. List your reasons, the value you want and documents the board can use to get there. Statute 77-1502 says late or incomplete protests are dismissed.

If the board rules against you, the Tax Equalization and Review Commission accepts appeals filed by August 24. A recent appraisal or a contractor's estimate for needed repairs makes a stronger case than opinion alone.

sections.h2: How the county tax sale works
sections.html:
Certificates are sold the first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse. The delinquent list is advertised for three consecutive weeks in February and posted online, and the county also posts a list of parcels that went unsold.

  • Bidders register by the Friday before the sale, for a $25 fee.
  • The county collects $25 on each certificate sold.
  • Owners may redeem for three years, with the certificate earning 14 percent.
  • Once three years pass with no redemption, the holder has six months to foreclose.

An unsold parcel is still delinquent. If yours is on that list, the tax remains owed and needs a plan.

Falls City Public Schools runs two elementary schools, a junior high and Falls City High School. Humboldt Table Rock Steinauer Public Schools, Auburn Public Schools, Johnson-Brock Public Schools and Pawnee City Public Schools also reach into the county, and Sacred Heart School in Falls City is a Catholic K to 12 school. Whichever district a house falls in drives its school levy, so check the district on your statement.
Buyers will ask about hail or wind damage, and a claim on file tells them more than the age of the roof does. Keep repair invoices and insurance paperwork together so you can answer plainly.

The title company gets the tax payoff from the treasurer and takes it out of your proceeds. You also owe the documentary stamp tax, which the register of deeds collects at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value on deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. The deed travels with Form 521.

If the house is inherited, in disrepair or behind on taxes, tell us the address and parcel number. We will go through the numbers with you, with no obligation. A cash sale skips the buyer's loan, so the schedule depends on title work and the payoff, not on a lender.

The order below fits Falls City, Humboldt and the villages alike.

  • Phone the treasurer at 402-245-3511 for the whole balance, drainage items broken out.
  • Check the assessor's record for the parcel, and ask about classification if it lies near reservation land.
  • See whether the parcel is on the county's list of unsold tax sale parcels.
  • Collect repair invoices and insurance claim papers so storm questions get plain answers.
  • Hand the title company the parcel number so payoff and deed are prepared together.

A brief call to each office usually shows which items apply to you.

Older owners mean some houses will move to heirs here. The tax calendar does not pause while an estate is settled, so May and September arrive on schedule for the heir too.

Be ready with papers showing who may sign, because the title company will ask. An heir in another state can handle most of this by phone and mail, since the treasurer, assessor and register of deeds all answer calls.

sections.h2: Why a cash buyer changes the schedule
sections.html:
No lender means no bank appraisal and no loan committee. For a house with deferred repairs, that removes the most common reason a closing collapses.

The stamp tax and every tax balance, drainage taxes included, still get settled at closing. What you gain is a calendar that follows title work and the payoff, and often your choice of closing day.

sections.h2: Why drainage taxes need a separate call
sections.html:
Drainage taxes are the one item on a Richardson County bill that the online payment system will not accept. A seller who pays everything else online and forgets the drainage line can leave a small balance sitting open at closing.

Call the treasurer at 402-245-3511 and ask for a payoff that spells out the drainage items on their own line. Hand that figure to the title company, and the balance gets paid from your proceeds with everything else.

After each March sale, the county posts the parcels that found no buyer. Being on that list does not erase the debt. Interest and the delinquent status carry on, and the same parcel can come back in the next sale. If you see your parcel there, treat it as a prompt to settle the balance or to close a sale soon.

faqs.q: When are Richardson County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half turns delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1, under Nebraska Statute 77-204.

faqs.q: Can I pay Richardson County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes, through MIPS Inc., at 2.35 percent for a card ($2.00 minimum) or $1.00 for an e-check. Drainage taxes are not payable online, so call 402-245-3511.

faqs.q: Where do I file a protest in Richardson County?
faqs.a: Send Form 422 to the County Clerk on or before June 30, one protest per parcel. Questions about the value go to the assessor at 402-245-4012.

faqs.q: When is the Richardson County tax sale?
faqs.a: The first Monday in March at 9:00 a.m. at the courthouse, after three weeks of advertising in February.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem after a Richardson County tax sale?
faqs.a: Three years. After that the certificate holder has six months to foreclose, and certificates carry 14 percent interest.
